subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a fixed 1 MiB public input limit, or should the resource-safety fix preserve current large-file acceptance through a different implementation boundary?
rationale: The cap intentionally changes an existing CLI input path, and repository policy treats new limits and removed fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive; mechanical review cannot choose the long-term contract.

options.title: Preserve current large-file behavior
options.body: Redesign the read/write path to bound memory without rejecting previously accepted large regular files, while safely rejecting non-regular handles.

options.title: Approve a documented 1 MiB contract
options.body: Accept the compatibility change, document the limit and recovery path, and add focused upgrade-facing proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the current implementation until a broader memory-wiki input-size policy is established.

recommendation.title: Preserve current large-file behavior
recommendation.body: Redesign the read/write path to bound memory without rejecting previously accepted large regular files, while safely rejecting non-regular handles.
